column1: # Game profile of Super Mario Bros. Wonder (Switch, base game v0 and update 1.2.1). This folder also holds the shader tables (generated by shader_split.py), pso_manifest.tsv and, not committed, c1_full.tsv and cb_extent.tsv

# Format: key <TAB> value; several values of one key are separated by spaces; one build row per version; comments must be on their own line. Rebuild the host after changing memory / NVN constants; after changing shader-related keys follow the chain procedure in AGENTS.md
# the game name is not kept here: the NSP script takes it from the NSP's control data (NACP)
# the value svcGetInfo(ProgramId) reports to the game (DM_PROGRAM_ID overrides it at run time)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# Tested on the record device (an iPhone 19,4, the Duo; update 1.2.1): the app runs today on the MTLDevice path, where every unseen shader pair compiles on the submit thread
# (the log's long frames carry 1,052 on-the-spot compiles over a session, up to a 1,014 ms frame; the same record replays the seed list's 760 lines in 0.06 s). The Metal 4 path
# gives iOS what the Mac already has: the pipeline archive made offline, the prepare step, the bases and the hybrid pipelines. The bases compile on the Mac for both families the
# profile names (3,697 bases: 67 MB for g19p, on Apple M2 Pro in 113 s); what the device finds missing it builds behind the prepare screen. Device checks still open: the archive
# opens on the Duo, the hybrids hold in gameplay, the prepare step's first-start build time (the fallback path when the archive is unusable) and the steady-state GPU cost
# the GPU families the offline archive compiles for (applegpu names): g18p = iPhone 17's A19 / A19 Pro; g19p = the Duo's (iPhone 19,4)

# build <version> <display version> <module>=<build ID>...: the NSP script accepts only these builds (fixed addresses do not hold on other builds); the host reports the display version by main's build ID
# version packed into the IPA by default
# the shader tables are the union of these versions (base game first): all of them are needed to build
# code modules rewritten and loaded (load order; rtld is replaced by the host)
# a path that must exist in the RomFS (tells whether the game files are in the right place)
# extensions zip stores without compressing (already compressed)
# ---- Memory (hle_svc.c; the reasons for the partition are in its comments) ----
# source groups: a path containing the first part goes to the second group (first match wins; shaders embedded in main always go to main, no match goes to other)
# description of the shader source in the map table header
